author: minnesotanpride
body:
It all amounts to your personal playstyle and what you like.  Do you like glass cannon play?  Thief tree classes might be your thing.  Like being an insurmountable wall?  Go warrior and make it to Gilgamesh.  Like being highly flexible in dishing damage but also healing and defense depending on what and who you are fighting?  Mage tree either Heretic or Deity.  Like stacking wild buffs and feeling like a dragon rider?  Go pet class up to Beowulf.  

Can't personally attest to amything but pet class except from my interactions with the other classes while leveling.  Am currently T10 Beowulf and absolutely loving it.  But I've built to it over the last three Tiers and have had lots of fights in all aspects of the game with it.  

Best thing I can say, just go with your gut and try something.  Really great thing about this game is you can always just buy the other classes of you want later and try them too.  Did that a few times when midgame trying to experiment.  Eventually fell in love with where I am now.  🤷‍♂️

author: No-Seaworthiness7013
body: There's a test client you can download that boosts you to 250 with enough orns to get all classes and a full load of gear and a bestiary with all the pets. Perhaps you could jump on that and give them a spin yourself and see which suits you best?

author: Pajamadoctor
body:
T9 baha is very strong. Omni is also very solid that tier. Like others have said, it depends on what you want to play.

In terms of efficiency, all players will need beo eventually for gaits.

There are one main pet at each tier that's a must, others are nice but not a necessity. At t9, it's crimson gazer (few good replacements depending on preference). At T10, it's fey cactus. 

In terms of ease, beo has more gear options and it is very very easy to do high damage with mediocre gear. You can get away using normal quality fey chimera gear and will be pretty successful in Pvp while farming for better options.

Imo, the only T10 class falling behind now is gilga. With the Ss3 nerf, not many people use it anymore. Beo does have a few difficulties with certain raids with parry but those are a lot more manageable once gunnr and snotra are available.

author: Master_Greg_Von
body: All tier 10 classes are equal and some are better than others at certain things but there is a balance. Baha at tier 10 you will eventually unlock all classes tho, but early tier 10 is generally easier with a pet class but less stable, however mid tier 10 a mage generally has an easier time doing endless and raids, but once you reach the end both classes are equally as good as each other

author: geoffnolan
body: I was mage until T9 and I switched to the thief line in T9. Make sure you have your gear upgraded before you make the switch, if you can. I'm now a Realmshifter in T10 and really still enjoying it. I may still make a deity build (I have all classes unlocked + altar of ascension), it's really up to me. As other commenters have stated, you will eventually unlock all classes.

author: Markemberke
body:
I've never tried mages, all I can say is that I love Beowulf, he's a beast. 💪 Even at the start of T10 you can easily slap and farm Morrigan, no problem. The DPS is high and constant. And you can just focus on yourself 100% in every fights. Also very strong in PvP and World Farming. Gauntlet is the only place where it can be annoying, when a mob is immune to your pet, so you have to leave the Gauntlet, get Niddhog for example, go back, kill that one mob, leave again, get Cactus back, go back and continue and hope that on the next floor isn't there the same mob, haha. :D

But other than Gauntlets, Beowulf is awesome, I love him. :3 It's just my experience with him and my opinion. 👍

author: NSA_Chatbot
body:
I was playing rogue-stream up until Nyx, then switched to Bahamut once I got some sweet drops that were too good to pass up.  

Beowulf is hilarious to play if, and only if, you enjoy random outcomes.  Most of the time you'll PvP people WAY ahead of you, but other times your pet is "yo just got back from the store, how did that fight ... aw you died?"  But then again, you've probably seen how much ward I have.  Fey Cactus is nearly unstoppable in PvP when a Beowolf has it.  There are ALWAYS builds that are better than you, even if you're better than someone else.  And RNG, what can you do? 

For raids, pets are outstanding.  You do have to let them do the work.  Your job is to buff, debuff, and ward.  If you've got nothing else, might as well hit them.  The only things that stop me during raids (at 226) are ultimate attacks, kingdom raid limits, or things outside of the game like "not feeling it" or "going to work".  Most of the time I don't even take damage except for Morrigan at about 4-5 million.  (Depending on the pet.  The Phoenixes are top-shelf, there's nothing else in the game that comes close in terms of raids.)  Am I doing the 1M-hits that we've seen Realmstrikes do?  Nope.  Just consistent damage, usually 100k a turn after the first 10 turns.  

Horde dungeons are *absolutely hilarious* with a Fey Cactus.  If you can get your ward up, you're good.  

Every class in the game should pick up Divine Bastion because the difference between 85% and 100% absorb is night and day.

author: petr1petr
body:
How can you feel that magic is less powerful? what makes you think so? imo it is not.. 

bahamut - the best thing is, that with crimson gazer, he is a beast in pvp. your tier people are going down very fast - only omnimancer has nice passive that may protect him from crimson gazer baha.

For anything else, you want to have different pet - so you need to switch pets for various aspects of game. Raids seemed slower, dungeons also - I played baha/mage - so I have been supporting my pet with my dmg - it was a lot of fun

Omnimancer - great class, very strong, can deal awesome dmg to morri, has omni spells - supergreat for endless. Has fey spells - thats where you can start seriously with crits. it also has great passives - manarush, steadfast, omnimancy - this allows you to tank monsters/bosses..

so baha/mage was fun to play, omnimancer was stronger - except for PvP

T10 - beo - cactus is beast in pvp - unless you meet someone with huge def. in dungeons, it is also great - especially if you go with friends or horde mode. it feels that it is slower in raids - the dmg is very consistent, but far from what I can do with heretic

heretic - shines in world, dungeons, raids - can do crazy dmg in pvp - but needs to survive :D Honestly, in PvP I have issues with strong boewulfs and strong shifters - anything else is OK..

also, currently, beo got a lot of love and updates made him stronger. 

Still, considering that pvp is just a small part of the game, I like heretic better. But beo is still a lot of fun - even without ascends..

author: Palocos
body:
My 2 cents. 
Bahamut is "better" than Omni and if you like mage I would advise to buy bahamut first, then omni, then god classes while at tier 9 and then save orns for heretic at tier 10.

The reason bahamut is better is that you can use any quality venin demonforged for maximum orns and xp and have more gear options and still do more damage than a well geared (not best geared) omnimancer. Omni also has weapons for farming but they are much harder to find and you need them to be ornate for damage. Going baha will allow you to farm much faster, provided you buy crimson gazer for world and pvp and nidhog for raids. The only thing omni does better is survivability in appolinon raid IF you have good gear (which you won't at level 200). 

Tier 10 is different. Heretic is really good for a lot of things and at T10 it's easier to farm orns and xp with any class. Beowulf might struggle with horde dungeons, hard endless and morrigan but the chimera pet hits like a mf bulldozer (provided the target doesn't resist dragon).
